content.thinking: I am examining NotFoundError and how other services use requireFound. I will also review transactions in the database client.

No transactions are currently active. better-sqlite3 with Drizzle supports the database.

A transaction is unnecessary because the tests are sequential. The merge replaces the source label with the target for every issue that had it, including archived ones. Issues that already carried both labels end up with the target exactly once. Issues without the source label remain unchanged.

The source label will be deleted entirely after the merge. The target label remains otherwise untouched. The function returns the target label and a count of issues relabeled. A Zod schema validates that the source and target IDs differ.

Zod 4 provides `check()` and `refine()` for validation.

Zod 4 `.refine()` returns a ZodEffects wrapper. The schema itself is unchanged.

ZodEffects was removed in Zod 4. `.refine()` likely returns the same schema type with a check attached.

The `toLabel` function omits `createdAt`. Returning the existing label object is safe.

The SQL merge algorithm queries `issue_labels` by org and source label to find affected issues.

The merge algorithm must respect the unique index on `issue_labels`. The safer approach is to delete source join rows only where the issue already carries the target label. Then update the remaining rows and drop the source label.

The exact SQL queries are now drafted. A subquery identifies issues that already carry the target label, and the update only changes rows for issues without it. The source label is deleted last. Counting rows by source label id directly yields the issue count, since the unique index on `issue_labels` guarantees at most one row per issue.

Archived issues are included in the merge because labels live on the join table and are not filtered by archive status.

The same-source-and-target case must be rejected before any writes, since it would be a no-op that deletes the label. Missing source or target labels return NotFoundError. The org-scoped lookup prevents cross-org lookups. Tenant scope errors block requests from actors outside the target organization. The permission model mirrors deleteLabel.

The merge logic should live in the label repository. The repository can return null when either label is missing, and the service layer can throw the error. This avoids a race condition between separate existence checks.

The `mergeLabels` service function is being drafted. It asserts tenant scope and the `project:archive` permission, rejects self-merges, and fetches both labels via `requireFound`.

The service function delegates the actual merge to `labelRepo.mergeLabelAssignments`, which returns the issue count. It then returns the target label and that count. Missing labels are rejected before any mutation. The entity name for `requireFound` is confirmed as "Label".

Cross-tenant permission checks throw PermissionDeniedError with reason denied_cross_tenant, not TenantScopeError.

I will call assertOrgScope before assertCan, following the deleteLabel pattern. Same-label rejection should throw an error before any mutation.

Checking error classes for NotFoundError, TenantScopeError, and PermissionDeniedError. Reviewing mergeLabelInto edge cases and schema validation with Node. Verifying Zod 4 refine output types.

Zod 4 refine preserves schema shape access. I'll verify count() behavior inside transactions and check the SQLite unique index on (issue_id, label_id) for merge conflicts.

The `findIssueById` function includes archived issues.

Writing and running the test file. Checking NotFoundError and TenantScopeError import paths. Verifying schema validation for duplicate IDs and invalid ULIDs. Confirming branded string equality works with Zod refine. Logging the ZodObject constructor name to verify mergeLabelsSchema type.

ULID casing is case-insensitive in the regex but not normalized, so differing cases are treated as distinct valid IDs. The service throws NotFoundError when a label is missing, and mergeLabelInto performs its own lookup. Duplicate source and target labels are rejected before any repository call.

Permission checks run before the same-ID guard. Unauthorized actors merging a label into itself would receive PermissionDeniedError instead of a generic Error.

Tenant scope validation runs first. A wrong organization always triggers TenantScopeError even when permission is also denied. Permission checks follow next. Missing labels return NotFoundError. Same-ID conflicts and missing-label conflicts are handled by whichever rule applies first.

Platform staff with a different organization still receive TenantScopeError, matching the deleteLabel behavior. The code is correct. I will write the smoke test and re-read the target label after merging to verify updatedAt.

The returned label is the pre-merge source object, so updatedAt will not match a subsequent fetch. I will return the freshly read target label instead, and requireFound will throw if the target was deleted.

I decided to keep the preloaded target label instead of re-fetching it, since both represent the same data. I will run the tests and check ESLint on the files.

Tests passed. The smoke test file will be deleted since it was not requested.

The smoke test covered the foreign target case. Schema output types for valid IDs still need verification, since tests used already-branded service IDs rather than schema parsing.

The `issuesRelabelled` count returns a number, not a bigint. A quick eslint check on the edited files will catch unused imports. All label-repository imports are used.

The repository throws a generic Error for missing labels, but the service checks first with NotFoundError. A mismatch between the find and merge queries is unlikely because they use the same query. The repository function name is flexible.

The repository function does not need to be exported. The code style matches the existing 2-space indentation, and the verbose comment will remain. Schema formatting is being double-checked.

Schema parsing and inference are covered. Role-based access checks are verified: members and viewers cannot merge labels, while admins and owners can. Same-ID rejection works correctly even when IDs differ only by type branding.
